subject: Pricing & commitment follow-up — Startup program / $/1M token qualification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@startupx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing follow-up + quick unit-econ questions

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a couple of qualification questions so we can put together a tailored proposal and any startup incentives.

Call recap:
- Primary use: real-time conversational experiences + nightly batch embedding pipelines for search/rerank.
- Expected steady-state volume: generation tokens ~50M–120M/month (varies by feature rollout).
- Embedding volume: ~3M–8M vectors/month (batch).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for online endpoints.

What we need from you (two quick items):
1) Budget range for inference (monthly run-rate) you’re comfortable committing to for the next 12 months (ballpark is fine — e.g., <$5k/mo, $5–20k/mo, $20–100k/mo, >$100k/mo).
2) Target unit economics: do you have a target $/1M tokens (or equivalent $/month) that makes the project attractive? If not, tell us the max acceptable monthly spend for the feature set above.

Why this matters: committed-use discounts and startup program incentives are structured around committed monthly spend and multi-month terms. With the volume you described we can show meaningful per-token reductions with a 6–12 month commitment. As a data point, our typical committed tiers (for reference only) are: 10% off at ~$10k/mo commit, 20% at ~$50k/mo, 30% at ~$150k/mo — we can also layer a 2-year incentive for deeper discounts.

We have a Startup Program that bundles a one-time credit + an additional year-first discount for qualifying early-stage companies; I attached the overview and a draft MAA with standard terms so your legal can scan.

If you can reply with budget band + any internal $/1M token target today, I’ll run numbers and get back with 2 options: a short-term starter commit (3–6 mo) and a 12–24 mo preferred commitment with the best unit economics.

Thanks — I’ll also loop Ben (solutions engineering) on the proposal to confirm perf assumptions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment: Startup_Program_Overview.pdf (summary of eligibility + credits)
Attachment: Draft_MAA_v1.docx (redlines welcome)

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@startupx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up + quick unit-econ questions

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the docs. Quick answers from our side:

- Budget band: currently planning for ~$10–25k/mo initially, with the possibility of stepping up to $40–80k/mo in 6–9 months if adoption goes well.
- Token economics: we don’t have a strict $/1M token target yet; finance is most concerned about the $/month impact. As a proxy, we’re looking for a path where production inference stays under ~$60k/mo for the full product (generations + embeddings) once at scale.

A few follow-ups:
1) Is the Startup Program eligibility based on funding stage / ARR? What’s the typical credit and discount structure?
2) For committed discounts, do you require an upfront prepay for the best tiers or is invoiced monthly with a true-up?
3) Any sample unit-econ calc you can share (e.g., for 50M tokens/month what does the bill look like before/after committed discounts + startup credit)?

CCing our CFO Sam Lee (sam.lee@startupx.com) who’ll be part of the procurement discussions.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Product, StartupX
alex.rivera@startupx.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up + quick unit-econ questions

Alex / Sam — thanks for the quick numbers, that helps a lot. Below I’ve laid out concrete examples so you can see the math; I kept model-agnostic assumptions for now and will firm up once Ben validates latency/throughput choices.

Assumptions (example calc):
- Generation volume: 50M tokens/month
- Embedding volume: 5M vectors/month (batch) — treat as equivalent to 5M tokens for rough unit-econ
- Baseline (on-hosted API, no discounts): $/1M tokens = $80 (example baseline rate for production-grade gen model) => monthly = (55M / 1M) * $80 = $4,400. (Note: this is illustrative — exact baseline depends on model and config)

Committed tiers (examples):
- Starter: 6-month commit at $10k/mo => ~10% off list pricing and priority capacity (no prepay required).
- Growth: 12-month commit at $50k/mo => ~20% off list + volume-based unit price reductions (billing monthly with quarterly true-up).
- Enterprise: 12–24 month commit $150k+/mo => ~30% off + additional SLO guarantees; typically includes option for monthly invoicing or annual prepay (higher discount for prepay).

Startup Program (qualifying early-stage):
- One-time credit: $15k applied to first invoices.
- Additional first-year discount: 15–25% off (depends on stage & ARR).
- Eligibility: Seed → Series A teams under $10M ARR (common case); we can take a quick eligibility form and confirm.

Example math (50M gen + 5M embedding = 55M tokens):
- No discounts: 55 * $80 = $4,400/mo
- With Growth commit (20% off): $4,400 * 0.8 = $3,520/mo
- With Startup credit applied once: first-month effective = $3,520 - $15,000 credit (credit will cover multiple months; remainder billed normally)

Notes: the numbers above are illustrative to show how committed discounts + startup credits stack. Ben will validate the model choice and performance overhead; once we agree on a target model we’ll provide a line-item quote with model-level $/1M tokens.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm eligibility for the Startup Program (I can run the eligibility check if you want).
- I’ll draft two proposals: (A) 6-mo starter commit at your $10–25k/mo band and (B) 12-mo Growth commit showing best unit economics + optional 2-yr add-on.
- If both look good, Ben and I can set a short technical call to lock perf assumptions BEFORE we pull together MAA / final commercial terms.

If you want, I can also produce a simple spreadsheet with the monthly run-rate for 50M, 80M, and 120M tokens showing list vs. committed vs. startup credits — will send that along with the proposals.

Would you like that spreadsheet? If so I’ll attach it to the proposals.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: Startup_Program_Overview.pdf
Attachment: Draft_MAA_v1.docx

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the proposals.
